findings: The implementation correctly follows Decision 0001 (Composable stations): the new content-film-review pipeline reuses existing stations (reviewer-design, reviewer-facts, approver, triage-human, publisher, observer) and is defined as a small JSON file ordering stations, not redefining them.

The declared evidence feature aligns with Decision 0003 (Production shape evidence): it enables work orders to reference evidence exercising the production shape (like finished films) rather than only source captures, addressing the gap demonstrated by wo-gh-21 and wo-gh-18.

The prepare_reviewer_design_step function correctly places packet assembly logic in anvil/runner.py (the runner module) where orchestration happens, not in station definitions, maintaining the separation of concerns between runner orchestration and station execution.

The implementation reuses the PNG security hardening from wo-gh-21 (size caps, CRC verification, decompression bounds checking, path validation) without weakening it, maintaining the security posture established in prior work.

The R4 implementation uses station_id.startswith('reviewer') as a convention-based check for adding the Declared evidence inputs section. This pattern is consistent with existing code at line 813 for output contracts, fitting the established architectural style.

The DeclaredEvidenceMissing exception is properly defined at the module level (line 30-32) alongside other domain exceptions (PacketBudgetError, ContactSheetError, AllowlistViolation, PathValidationError), following the project's error handling pattern.
The WorkOrder model's evidence_images field (already present at line 46 in model.py) is correctly extended without modifying the model structure, maintaining backward compatibility.
Tests follow the established pattern from test_astra_consumption.py with small PNG fixtures, deterministic execution, no model calls, and no network, consistent with the project's test architecture.
The CHANGELOG entry correctly documents the feature in the Unreleased section following the project's changelog format and style.
Nine pipelines now exist (verified in pipelines/ directory), correctly increasing from the previous eight, with content-film-review.json following the same structure as other pipeline definitions.
